name: clearcote-mcp
description: Drive the Clearcote Chromium browser from any MCP client: read pages, click, fill, screenshot.
long_description: Runs the open-source Clearcote Chromium browser locally and gives your agent about 20 tools to navigate, read pages as Markdown, extract, click, fill, screenshot and keep sessions. `get_cdp_endpoint` hands the same browser to Playwright, Puppeteer, browser-use or Crawl4AI. The fingerprint is set in Chromium's C++, so no JavaScript stealth plugins are needed. The first run downloads the browser and verifies its SHA-256.

tools.name: navigate
tools.description: Navigate the current tab to a URL. Returns the resolved url, title, http_status and page_state (see read_page).

tools.name: read_page
tools.description: Read the current page (or navigate to `url` first) as Markdown (default), its visible "text", or "both". Also returns http_status (the shown document's; null if unknown) and page_state: "blocked" (HTTP 401, 403, 429 or 503), "empty" (under 20 characters of visible text) or "ok". Long fields are cut; markdown_truncated / text_truncated say so.

tools.name: get_page_html
tools.description: Get the HTML of the current page (or navigate to `url` first), inside the untrusted-content fence.

tools.name: page_elements
tools.description: List the interactive elements (links, buttons, inputs) on the page, one JSON object per line, each with a selector.

tools.name: click
tools.description: Click an element by CSS selector or by visible text (navigate to `url` first if given).

tools.name: fill_field
tools.description: Fill an input matched by selector, label, placeholder, or name.

tools.name: press_key
tools.description: Press a key on the current page, e.g. 'Enter', 'Tab', 'Control+A'.

tools.name: evaluate_js
tools.description: Evaluate a JavaScript expression in the page and return its (JSON-serializable) result, as JSON text inside the untrusted-content fence.

tools.name: wait_for
tools.description: Wait until a selector appears (up to timeout_ms).

tools.name: current_page
tools.description: Return the current tab's url + title.

tools.name: screenshot_page
tools.description: Screenshot the current page (or navigate to `url` first), saved under the sandbox dir. Up to 200 KB it is also returned as an image; a bigger one only as its file path (inline: false).

tools.name: save_page_pdf
tools.description: Save the current page as a PDF (headless only). Saved under the sandbox dir.

tools.name: get_cookies
tools.description: Get cookies for the current context (optionally filtered to `url`). Each cookie's name, value, domain and path are the site's, each between untrusted-content tags on one line.

tools.name: list_tabs
tools.description: List open tabs (index, url, title, which is current).

tools.name: new_tab
tools.description: Open a new tab (optionally navigate it) and make it current.

tools.name: close_tab
tools.description: Close the tab at `index` (from list_tabs).

tools.name: save_profile
tools.description: Save cookies + storage state to a named profile under the sandbox dir.

tools.name: load_profile
tools.description: Restore cookies + storage from a named profile (see save_profile).

tools.name: get_egress_info
tools.description: Report the browser's public egress IP (through any configured proxy) + the active persona.

tools.name: get_cdp_endpoint
tools.description: Return the stealth browser's raw CDP endpoint so ANY other client (Playwright / Puppeteer / browser-use / Crawl4AI / Stagehand) can attach to the SAME browser with `connect_over_cdp`, keeping the stealth persona. This is the whole point of the drop-in model.

fingerprint.title: Fingerprint seed
fingerprint.description: Seed for one stable identity (the same seed is the same device on every run). Empty: a new identity each run.

platform.title: Platform persona
platform.description: windows, linux, macos or android. Empty: this machine's platform.

geoip.title: GeoIP
geoip.description: 1: timezone, locale and WebRTC IP follow the proxy's exit IP. 0: off.

cloud.title: Cloud mode
cloud.description: 1: the browser is a hosted Clearcote session (needs an API key).

api_key.title: Clearcote API key
api_key.description: For cloud mode and the run_task tool. Not needed for the local browser.
